title_en: China Development Bank v. Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd., New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd., New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High Voltage Disconnector Co., Ltd., Shenyang Beifu Machinery Manufacturing Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over loan contract and right of revocation
ruling_gist_en: Article 74 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides that where a debtor transfers property at a price that is obviously unreasonably low, thereby harming the creditor, and the transferee knows of such circumstances, the creditor may request the people's court to revoke the debtor's act of transferring the property.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over loan contract; dispute over right of revocation; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Liaoning Province; legal person; financial institution; Contract Law; debtor transfers property at an obviously unreasonably low price; elements of creditor's right of revocation; determination of transferee's knowledge of circumstances; partial support; loan contract; equity transfer; asset transfer at low price
full_text_en:
China Development Bank v. Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear Co., Ltd., New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High-Voltage Switchgear Co., Ltd., New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High-Voltage Disconnector Co., Ltd., Shenyang Beifu Machinery Manufacturing Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over loan contract and right of revocation

[Ruling Summary]

Pursuant to Article 74 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where a debtor transfers property at an obviously unreasonable low price, thereby causing damage to a creditor, and the transferee knows of such circumstances, the creditor may petition the People's Court to revoke the debtor's act of transferring the property.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 23

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Development Bank, domiciled at No. 29, Fuwai Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Chen Yuan, President of the Bank.
Agent ad litem: Bai Qiang, Staff of Liaoning Branch of the Bank.
Agent ad litem: Chen Liyang, Attorney at Beijing Dali Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 39, Shen Railway, Dadong District, Shenyang, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Baozhu, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Xi Zhaoyang, Attorney at Liaoning Tongfang Law Firm, Beijing Branch.
Agent ad litem: Wang Xiaoxuan, Attorney at Liaoning Tongfang Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High-Voltage Switchgear Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 14-5, 5th Road, Shenyang Economic and Technological Development Zone, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Zhou Ye, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Rong Bing, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Liu Lichao, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High-Voltage Disconnector Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 39, Century Road, Hunnan High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, Shenyang, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Bing, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Yan, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xie Yang, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenyang Beifu Machinery Manufacturing Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 14-5, 5th Road, Shenyang Economic and Technological Development Zone, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Jiang Hai, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Yan, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xie Yang, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenyang Dongli Logistics Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 35-1, Huahai Road, Shenyang Economic and Technological Development Zone, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Lin Zhiwu, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Yan, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xie Yang, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 78, Hunnan High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, Shenyang, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Zhen, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Yan, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xie Yang, Attorney at Beijing Yida Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Shenyang Transformer Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 18, Beier Zhong Road, Tiexi District, Shenyang, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Luo Guiliang, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wei Lijun, Legal Counsel of the Company.

Defendant at First Instance: Northeast Construction and Installation Engineering Corporation, domiciled at No. 187, Taiyuan South Street, Heping District, Shenyang, Liaoning Province.
Legal Representative: Li Ruihan.

The appellant, China Development Bank (hereinafter referred to as CDB), appealed to this Court against the Civil Judgment (2004) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 802 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case of dispute over loan contracts and right of revocation with the appellees Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear), New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High-Voltage Switchgear Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as New Northeast Electric), New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High-Voltage Disconnector Co., Ltd. (formerly Shenyang Xintai High-Voltage Electric Co., Ltd., name changed to current name on December 21, 2005, hereinafter referred to as Xintai High-Voltage), Shenyang Beifu Machinery Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (formerly Shenyang Chengtai Energy Power Co., Ltd., name changed to current name on December 28, 2006, hereinafter referred to as Chengtai Energy), Shenyang Dongli Logistics Co., Ltd. (formerly Shenyang Xintai Warehousing Logistics Co., Ltd., name changed to current name on December 28, 2006, hereinafter referred to as Xintai Warehousing), Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Northeast Electric), and the defendants at first instance Shenyang Transformer Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenyang Transformer) and Northeast Construction and Installation Engineering Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Northeast Construction and Installation). After accepting the case, this Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Zhang Shuming, Acting Judges Yin Yuan and Sha Ling to hear the case, with Zhao Suijun serving as court clerk. The case is now concluded.

The facts found by the court of first instance are as follows:

On August 21, 1998, CDB and Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear entered into a Capital Construction Loan Contract stipulating that Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear would borrow RMB 153 million from CDB for civil engineering works and equipment purchase, with a loan term of nine years, i.e., from July 1, 1998 to July 1, 2007, at an annual interest rate of 8.01%. CDB was to disburse RMB 40 million from July to December 1998, RMB 65 million in 1999, and RMB 48 million in 2000. Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear was to repay the principal and interest of the above amounts to CDB in seven installments from November 2001 to November 2007. During the term of this contract, should Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear undergo changes in business methods or property rights such as contracting, leasing, merger, consolidation, division, joint venture, association, shareholding reform, optimization of capital structure, or asset restructuring, it was required to notify CDB 60 days in advance and obtain CDB's written consent or reach a new agreement with CDB; otherwise, CDB had the right to recover the loan ahead of schedule. The contract also stipulated other rights and obligations of the parties and liability for breach. On the same day, CDB, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear, and Shenyang Transformer entered into a Guarantee Contract, whereby Shenyang Transformer agreed to assume joint and several liability for the entire principal and interest of the loan under this contract. After the contract was signed, CDB disbursed the loan to Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear in installments. Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear did not dispute RMB 102 million of the disbursed amounts. As for the remaining RMB 51 million, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear argued that CDB had not disbursed it. The reason was that a loan transfer certificate from China Construction Bank Shenyang Tiexi Sub-branch for RMB 30 million was not an original, and the copy itself did not show the transfer date; it should not be considered as a loan disbursed to Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear under this contract. As for RMB 20 million, the evidence provided by CDB was not a loan certificate and could not prove that CDB had actually disbursed RMB 20 million to Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear. CDB argued that Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear had affixed its seal to a confirmation statement to CDB acknowledging that as of December 31, 2002, it still owed CDB RMB 140 million, thus CDB had disbursed the loan as agreed.

After repaying the RMB 5 million loan due in 2001 and the RMB 8 million loan due in 2002 to CDB, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear failed to repay the remaining principal and interest.

On May 13, 2003, CDB and Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear entered into a Short-Term Loan Contract stipulating that Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear would borrow RMB 10 million from CDB for a term of one year, i.e., from May 13, 2003 to May 12, 2004, at an annual interest rate of 5.31%. Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear was to repay the principal and interest of the above amount to CDB on May 12, 2004. The contract also stipulated other rights and obligations of the parties and liability for breach. On the same day, CDB and Northeast Construction and Installation entered into a Guarantee Contract, whereby Northeast Construction and Installation agreed to assume joint and several liability for the entire principal and interest of the loan under this contract. After the contract was signed, CDB disbursed RMB 10 million to Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear. Upon the expiration of the contract, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear failed to repay the principal and interest of this loan.

Additionally, it was found that: 1. On May 15, 2003, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear invested physical assets worth USD 1.25 million in the establishment of New Northeast Electric as a joint venture with others; 2. On February 26, 2004, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear invested physical assets worth USD 16 million in the establishment of Xintai High-Voltage as a joint venture with others, and Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear obtained 74.4% of the equity in Xintai High-Voltage; 3. On March 15, 2004, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear invested physical assets worth RMB 85,510,600 in the establishment of Chengtai Energy as a joint venture with others, and Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear obtained 95% of the equity in Chengtai Energy; 4. On March 24, 2004, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear invested physical assets and land worth RMB 161,605,900 in the establishment of Xintai Warehousing as a joint venture with others, and Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear obtained 95% of the equity in Xintai Warehousing.

On March 19, 2004, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric entered into an equity transfer agreement, whereby Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear transferred its 74.4% equity in Xintai High-Voltage to Northeast Electric. On March 24, 2004, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric entered into an equity transfer agreement, whereby Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear transferred its 95% equity in Chengtai Energy to Northeast Electric. On March 25, 2004, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric entered into an equity transfer agreement, whereby Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear transferred its 95% equity in Xintai Warehousing to Northeast Electric. On April 7, 2004, Northeast Electric transferred its 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng Communication Equipment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenyang Tiansheng) to Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear as consideration for acquiring Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's 74.4% equity in Xintai High-Voltage. On April 14, 2004, Northeast Electric transferred its claims against Northeast Transmission and Substation Equipment Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Northeast Transmission and Substation) in the amount of RMB 76.66 million plus interest as consideration for acquiring Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's 95% equity in Chengtai Energy and 95% equity in Xintai Warehousing.

CDB argued that the production equipment invested by Northeast Electric into Shenyang Tiansheng had been used for a long time, and the 98.5% equity had no actual value. The assets invested by Northeast Electric into Shenyang Tiansheng as appraised at RMB 130,033,900 in the Liao Sheng Ping Bao Zi (2004) No. 017 appraisal report were inaccurate. Northeast Electric argued that CDB had no evidence proving that the Liao Sheng Ping Bao Zi (2004) No. 017 appraisal report was inaccurate. Moreover, on August 13, 2006, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear had transferred the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenyang Dejia) for RMB 130 million, and this transaction was valid.

CDB argued that Northeast Electric's claims against Northeast Transmission and Substation in the amount of RMB 76.66 million plus interest were non-performing assets, as the Civil Enforcement Ruling (2000) Shen Xing Zhi Zi No. 20 of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court had already terminated the enforcement due to Northeast Transmission and Substation's lack of property available for enforcement. Northeast Electric argued that according to the statement of main claims and equity issued by Northeast Transmission and Substation, it had a large number of equity interests in several subsidiaries and held significant external claims. Northeast Electric had already realized RMB 10,637,273.9 from Northeast Transmission and Substation. After Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear acquired the claims against Northeast Transmission and Substation, it had partially realized RMB 4 million in claims. CDB could not conclude that Northeast Electric's claims against Northeast Transmission and Substation were inferior-quality claims merely because one ruling had not been enforced. Further, the land use rights included in Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's capital contribution to Chengtai Energy and Xintai Warehousing belonged to Northeast Electric; therefore, the actual value of the equity in Chengtai Energy and Xintai Warehousing held by Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear was RMB 91,258,500.

On May 31, 2004, CDB filed a lawsuit with the Beijing High People's Court, requesting: 1. an order that Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear pay principal of RMB 150 million in loans and interest; 2. an order that Shenyang Transformer assume joint and several liability for the principal of RMB 140 million in loans and interest; 3. an order that Northeast Construction and Installation assume joint and several liability for the principal of RMB 10 million in loans and interest; 4. a declaration that the equity transfer contracts between Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric were void; 5. an order that New Northeast Electric, Xintai High-Voltage, Chengtai Energy, Xintai Warehousing, and Northeast Electric assume joint and several liability for Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's debts; and 6. an order that the defendants bear the litigation costs. During the trial, CDB argued that since Northeast Electric had transferred the equity it acquired from Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear to a third party, Northeast Electric should bear compensation liability for the portion it could not return.

It was also found that on March 31, 2005, CDB filed a lawsuit with the Liaoning High People's Court, requesting the revocation of the equity transfers between Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric concerning Xintai High-Voltage, Chengtai Energy, and Xintai Warehousing. The Liaoning High People's Court held that CDB's lawsuit against Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric in the Beijing High People's Court and its lawsuit in the Liaoning High People's Court were both based on the same legal facts, namely the transfer of 74.4% equity in Xintai High-Voltage, 95% equity in Chengtai Energy, and 95% equity in Xintai Warehousing between Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear and Northeast Electric, albeit with different specific claims. Since the Beijing High People's Court had accepted the case earlier, the case should be transferred to the Beijing High People's Court for consolidated hearing. On November 27, 2006, the Liaoning High People's Court issued a ruling transferring the case to the Beijing High People's Court, but did not transfer the case acceptance fee. After acceptance, the Beijing High People's Court consolidated the transferred case with the present case for trial.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the Loan Contracts, the Guarantee Contracts, the Liao Sheng Ping Bao Zi (2004) No. 017 Appraisal Report, the business registration archives of New Northeast Electric, the business registration archives of Xintai High-Voltage, the contract for Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's transfer of equity in Xintai High-Voltage, the business registration archives of Chengtai Energy, the contract for Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's transfer of equity in Chengtai Energy, the business registration archives of Xintai Warehousing, the contract for Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's transfer of equity in Xintai Warehousing, the contract for Northeast Electric's transfer of equity in Shenyang Tiansheng, the announcement of Northeast Electric's acquisition of equity, the business registration archives of Shenyang Tiansheng, the civil judgment and civil ruling of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court, the list of loan principal and interest, loan certificates, repayment certificates, the civil ruling (2005) Liao Min San Chu Zi No. 21 of the Liaoning High People's Court, and the trial transcripts.

The court of first instance held that the two loan contracts entered into between CDB and Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear, and the two guarantee contracts entered into between CDB and Shenyang Transformer and Northeast Construction and Installation, reflected the true intent of the parties and did not violate mandatory provisions of national laws and regulations, and thus should be deemed lawful and valid. Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear failed to notify CDB in advance and obtain its consent as required by the contract regarding changes in its property rights. Therefore, CDB was entitled to accelerate the loan recovery as stipulated in the contract. Since Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear affixed its seal to the confirmation statement acknowledging that as of December 31, 2002, it still owed CDB RMB 140 million, the court confirmed that CDB had disbursed a total of RMB 163 million. Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear should bear the liability to repay the principal and interest of RMB 150 million in arrears. The court supported CDB's request for an order that Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear pay the loan principal and interest.

The guarantee contract between CDB and Shenyang Transformer explicitly stipulated that Shenyang Transformer would assume joint and several liability for the principal and interest of RMB 153 million in loans. The guarantee contract between CDB and Northeast Construction and Installation explicitly stipulated that Northeast Construction and Installation would assume joint and several liability for the principal and interest of RMB 10 million in loans. Therefore, Shenyang Transformer and Northeast Construction and Installation should each bear corresponding joint and several liability as stipulated in the guarantee contracts.

The act of Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear in contributing capital to establish New Northeast Electric, Xintai High-Voltage, Chengtai Energy, and Xintai Warehousing was a normal corporate investment by shareholders. It merely changed the form of Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's property from tangible assets to equity, without reducing its liable property or impairing its capacity to satisfy debts. The transfer by Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear of its equity in Xintai High-Voltage, Chengtai Energy, and Xintai Warehousing was an act of disposing of its own assets, unrelated to the independently legal entities Xintai High-Voltage, Chengtai Energy, and Xintai Warehousing. Therefore, CDB's request that New Northeast Electric, Xintai High-Voltage, Chengtai Energy, and Xintai Warehousing assume joint and several liability had no factual or legal basis and was not supported by the court.

Regarding Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear's exchange of its 74.4% equity in Xintai High-Voltage for Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear had initially obtained the 74.4% equity in Xintai High-Voltage by contributing USD 16 million. During the trial, Northeast Electric submitted evidence that on August 13, 2006, Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear had transferred the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia for RMB 130 million. Therefore, CDB's assertion that the consideration for this equity exchange was seriously disproportionate was insufficiently supported by evidence and was not accepted by the court.

Regarding the issue of Shenyang Gaokai exchanging its 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing for the debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission to Northeast Electric. Because Shenyang Gaokai had acquired 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy by contributing physical assets valued at RMB 85,510,600, and had acquired 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing by contributing physical assets and land valued at RMB 161,605,900. Shenyang Gaokai's capital contributions, as recorded in the book assets alone, amounted to RMB 247,116,500. However, the debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission to Northeast Electric, which was used to exchange for the aforesaid equity, could not be enforced against Northeast Power Transmission as it had no property available for execution. The Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province had already issued a ruling terminating the execution. As there is still no evidence proving that the debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission to Northeast Electric could be realized, it should be determined that this debt is a non-performing asset. Northeast Electric used this non-performing asset as consideration to exchange for the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing held by Shenyang Gaokai. The consideration was severely imbalanced, resulting in the improper reduction of the liable property of Shenyang Gaokai as a legal person entity serving as general security for its civil activities. Both parties were fully aware of this consequence. The equity exchange between Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric infringed upon the interests of creditors and satisfied the statutory conditions under which creditors may exercise the right of revocation as provided in the Contract Law of the PRC. China Development Bank's claim for revocation of the equity exchange contract between Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric is therefore established and should be supported. Given that China Development Bank requests that Northeast Electric return the equity in Shenyang Gaokai obtained thereby, and assume compensation liability for any portion unable to be returned. Therefore, under the principle of mutual restitution, Northeast Electric should return the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing obtained to Shenyang Gaokai, and Shenyang Gaokai should return the debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission to Northeast Electric. If Northeast Electric is unable to return, it shall compensate Shenyang Gaokai for losses up to RMB 247,116,500. Additionally, the dispute over the right of revocation in case (2005) Liao San Min Chu Zi No. 21, transferred by the Liaoning High People's Court, has been consolidated with this case for trial, and no case acceptance fee has been collected for that case. China Development Bank should request the Liaoning High People's Court to refund the case acceptance fee paid for filing that case. In summary, the court of first instance, pursuant to Articles 74, 204, 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 18 of the Security Law of the PRC, and Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered a default judgment as follows: 1. Shenyang Gaokai shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, repay to China Development Bank the principal loan of RMB 150,000,000 and interest and penalty interest (for RMB 140,000,000, calculated from December 1, 2002, to the date of actual payment, at the standard for overdue penalty interest set by the People's Bank of China for the same period; for RMB 10,000,000, calculated from May 13, 2003, to May 12, 2004, at an annual rate of 5.31%, and from May 13, 2004, to the date of actual payment, at the standard for overdue penalty interest set by the People's Bank of China for the same period). If Shenyang Gaokai fails to perform the payment obligation within the period specified in the judgment, it shall, in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance; 2. Shenyang Transformer shall assume joint and several guaranty liability for the principal loan of RMB 140,000,000 and penalty interest among the aforesaid debts of Shenyang Gaokai, and shall have the right to seek recourse from Shenyang Gaokai to the extent of the guaranty performed; 3. Northeast Jian'an shall assume joint and several guaranty liability for the principal loan of RMB 10,000,000, interest, and penalty interest among the aforesaid debts of Shenyang Gaokai, and shall have the right to seek recourse from Shenyang Gaokai to the extent of the guaranty performed; 4. The contract for equity exchange whereby Northeast Electric exchanged its debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission for the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing held by Shenyang Gaokai is rescinded; 5. Northeast Electric shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, return the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing to Shenyang Gaokai; if Northeast Electric is unable to return, it shall compensate Shenyang Gaokai for losses up to RMB 247,116,500; Shenyang Gaokai shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, return the debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission to Northeast Electric; if Shenyang Gaokai is unable to return, it shall compensate Northeast Electric for losses up to RMB 76,660,000; 6. The other claims of China Development Bank are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 768,729.62 and preservation fee of RMB 759,239.62 shall be borne jointly by Shenyang Gaokai and Shenyang Transformer in the amount of RMB 1,500,000 (to be paid within seven days after the judgment takes effect), and jointly by Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Jian'an in the amount of RMB 27,969.24 (to be paid within seven days after the judgment takes effect).

China Development Bank, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Beijing High People's Court, appealed to this Court, stating: 1. On March 19, 2004, Shenyang Gaokai exchanged its 74.4% equity in Xin Tai High Voltage for Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng. This was an act of malicious collusion between the parties to transfer assets and evade bank financial claims, which seriously harmed the interests of all creditors including China Development Bank, and should be an invalid contract. The original judgment, relying solely on the fact that Shenyang Gaokai transferred its 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia for RMB 130,000,000 (without relevant evidence being cross-examined in court), determined that Northeast Electric had paid consideration to Shenyang Gaokai in the equity exchange, which lacks sufficient basis. 2. Based on the facts already ascertained at first instance, Northeast Electric exchanged its debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission for the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing held by Shenyang Gaokai. Since Northeast Electric used the debt and interest of RMB 76,660,000 owed by Northeast Power Transmission as the transaction consideration, and since this debt had no possibility of realization, the equity exchange was still an act of malicious collusion to transfer assets and evade bank financial claims, and the equity transfer contract should be invalid. 3. From May 2003 to March 2004, Shenyang Gaokai used its high-quality assets to form four companies, including New Northeast Electric, through joint ventures with others, stripping the company's high-quality assets to the newly formed companies while leaving the debts with the original enterprise, objectively rendering itself incapable of production and debt repayment. Under the principle of enterprise legal person property and Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring, the four companies, New Northeast Electric, Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing, should assume joint and several liability within the scope of the property they respectively received. Furthermore, Northeast Electric, as the original capital contributor of Shenyang Gaokai, failed to fulfill its full capital contribution obligation and therefore should assume joint and several liability for Shenyang Gaokai's debts to the extent of the shortfall in registered capital. In summary, China Development Bank requests: 1. To set aside items 4 and 6 of the original civil judgment; 2. To declare invalid or rescind the contract for equity exchange whereby Northeast Electric exchanged its 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng for Shenyang Gaokai's 74.4% equity in Xin Tai High Voltage; 3. To declare invalid the contract for equity exchange whereby Northeast Electric exchanged its debt of RMB 76,660,000 and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission for Shenyang Gaokai's 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing; 4. To order the appellees, New Northeast Electric, Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, Xin Tai Warehousing, and Northeast Electric, to assume joint and several liability for Shenyang Gaokai's debts.

The appellee Shenyang Gaokai responded as follows: 1. Regarding the facts of the loan in this case. (1) After the loan contract in this case was signed, China Development Bank paid RMB 102,000,000 to Shenyang Gaokai, and the remaining RMB 51,000,000 has not been paid to date. Therefore, the portion of its claims exceeding RMB 102,000,000 should not be supported. (2) Among the loan vouchers provided by China Development Bank, some entrusted loan vouchers show the payee as Shenyang High-Voltage Switchgear Factory, not the respondent Shenyang Gaokai, and cannot prove that China Development Bank disbursed the loan to Shenyang Gaokai. Additionally, the vouchers for entrusted loans disbursed by China Development Bank through the Shenyang Tiexi Sub-branch of China Construction Bank bear two transfer stamps, which does not comply with banking operational regulations, and the transfer time also does not match the loan contract. (3) Shenyang Gaokai did not misappropriate China Development Bank's loan proceeds, nor did it commit any material breach of the provisions in Article 7, paragraphs 9 and 10 of the Long-term Loan Contract. Although there was a temporary default on interest, this was a normal operational risk for the company, and the loan contract could continue to be performed. 2. Shenyang Gaokai did not engage in any act of maliciously stripping assets. (1) Shenyang Gaokai's outward investment to form the four companies including New Northeast Electric was a lawful investment act by the company and did not result in a reduction of assets. Shenyang Gaokai's transfer of its equity in New Northeast Electric, Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing was an act of disposing of its own assets and was unrelated to those four companies. The original judgment's finding that these four companies, as independent legal persons, do not assume joint and several repayment liability is correct. As for Article 10 of the Several Opinions of the Shenyang Administration for Industry and Commerce on Promoting the Revitalization of the Old Industrial Base, cited by China Development Bank, which provides that the total outward investment of a domestic limited liability company is not limited to 50% of its net assets, Shenyang Gaokai's outward investment amount, although exceeding the 50% limit under the Company Law, was based on preferential policies for specific regions, and there was no malicious intent as alleged by China Development Bank. (2) Shenyang Gaokai's transfer of equity in Xin Tai High Voltage was lawful and valid. According to the Asset Appraisal Report (Liao Sheng Ping Bao Zi [2004] No. 017) issued by Liaoning Shenghua Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd., the value of that equity was RMB 130,000,000, equivalent to the value of USD 16,000,000 for the equity in Xin Tai High Voltage held by Northeast Electric. Thus, the equity transfer was lawful and valid. After Shenyang Gaokai obtained 98.48% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng, it transferred that equity to Shenyang Dejia for RMB 130,000,000, which also demonstrates the actual value of that equity. The original court correctly determined that there was no serious imbalance of consideration in that equity exchange. (3) The equity-for-debt exchange between Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric was for operational needs, and the exchanged debt was not a non-collectible inferior debt as claimed by Shenyang Gaokai. The debt of RMB 76,660,000 principal and corresponding interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission, which Northeast Electric paid as consideration to Shenyang Gaokai, was a fully realizable high-quality debt. (4) Shenyang Gaokai obtained reasonable consideration for the transfer of equity in Xin Tai High Voltage, and there was no malicious collusion. 3. The original court correctly applied the law. The original court correctly determined that this case should not apply the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring but rather the relevant provisions of the Contract Law. The companies invested in and established by Shenyang Gaokai are independent legal persons and should not bear any liability for Shenyang Gaokai's debts. In summary, the appellee requests that the appeal of the appellant China Development Bank be dismissed.

The appellee New Northeast Electric responded as follows: 1. New Northeast Electric is not required to assume joint and several liability for the loan contract dispute between Shenyang Gaokai and China Development Bank. (1) New Northeast Electric is an independent company legal person, enjoying civil rights and undertaking civil obligations independently in accordance with law. (2) The loan relationship between Shenyang Gaokai and China Development Bank arose from the loan contract between them and has no legal binding effect on New Northeast Electric. (3) After Shenyang Gaokai made its capital contribution to New Northeast Electric, that portion of assets became independent legal person property owned by New Northeast Electric as an independent civil subject. (4) The Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring is intended for the trial of civil dispute cases arising in the process of enterprise ownership system reform. Shenyang Gaokai completed its enterprise ownership system reform as early as 1993 and established a limited liability company. The loan dispute between China Development Bank and Shenyang Gaokai arose on May 31, 2004, which clearly does not fall within the scope of civil disputes arising during enterprise ownership system reform, and therefore this interpretation should not apply. Moreover, this interpretation was enacted in 2003, while the loan relationship between China Development Bank and Shenyang Gaokai was formed in 1998. Under the principle that laws shall not be retroactive, it should not apply to this case. 2. New Northeast Electric is not a proper defendant in this case. In summary, the appellee requests that China Development Bank's appeal for New Northeast Electric to assume joint and several liability for Shenyang Gaokai's debts be dismissed.

The appellees Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, Xin Tai Warehousing, and Northeast Electric responded as follows: 1. Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing are not required to assume joint and several liability for the loan contract dispute between Shenyang Gaokai and China Development Bank. First, Shenyang Gaokai, Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing are all independent company legal persons, each independently enjoying civil rights and undertaking civil obligations in accordance with law. Second, the loan relationship between Shenyang Gaokai and China Development Bank arose from the loan contract between them and has no legal binding effect on Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing. Third, after Shenyang Gaokai made its capital contributions to Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing, those assets became independent legal person property owned by these entities as independent civil subjects. Finally, the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring is intended for the trial of civil dispute cases arising in the process of enterprise ownership system reform. Shenyang Gaokai completed its enterprise ownership system reform as early as 1993 and established a limited liability company. The loan dispute between China Development Bank and Shenyang Gaokai arose on May 31, 2004, which clearly does not fall within the scope of civil disputes arising during enterprise ownership system reform, and therefore this interpretation should not apply. 2. Xin Tai High Voltage, Cheng Tai Energy, and Xin Tai Warehousing are not proper defendants in this case. 3. China Development Bank's request for Northeast Electric to assume corresponding joint and several liability for insufficient capital contribution lacks factual and legal basis. (1) China Development Bank has not provided any evidence to prove that Northeast Electric made an insufficient capital contribution. Moreover, Northeast Electric, as the original capital contributor of Shenyang Gaokai, has long completed its capital contribution obligation. (2) According to the Company Law of China and other relevant legal provisions, a shareholder who fails to make sufficient capital contribution shall make up the shortfall to the company and bear liability for breach of contract to other shareholders who have made full contributions, but it does not directly assume liability to creditors, let alone joint and several liability. 4. The equity transfer contract between Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai was a normal market transaction, involving neither malicious collusion nor infringement on the interests of third parties. (1) The exchange of Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng for Shenyang Gaokai's 74.4% equity in Xin Tai High Voltage was fair and reasonable. (a) Regarding the value of the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng: the appraisal report issued by the appraisal department can prove that Northeast Electric's capital contribution to Shenyang Tiansheng was valued at RMB 130,000,000. On August 11, 2006, Shenyang Gaokai transferred the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng for RMB 130,000,000. The equity change registration was completed on August 13, 2006, and the full transfer price has been paid. This fact can prove that as of August 11, 2006, the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng was valued at RMB 130,000,000 (approximately USD 16,250,000). (b) Regarding the value of the 74.4% equity in Xin Tai High Voltage: on February 26, 2004, Shenyang Gaokai contributed physical assets appraised at USD 16,000,000 as capital to jointly establish Xin Tai High Voltage with others, thus the 74.4% equity in Xin Tai High Voltage can be considered to be valued at USD 16,000,000. (c) The 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng and the 74.4% equity in Xin Tai High Voltage were of comparable value, and there was no malicious collusion to harm the interests of third parties. (2) Northeast Electric's exchange of its debt of RMB 76,660,000 and corresponding interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission for Shenyang Gaokai's 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing. (a) Regarding the value of the RMB 76,660,000 debt and interest owed by Northeast Power Transmission: the RMB 76,660,000 debt and corresponding interest were worth over RMB 80,000,000. According to the [2004] Shen Fa Zhi Zi No. 498 ruling, Northeast Electric, as a creditor of Northeast Power Transmission, had already realized RMB 10,637,273.90 of the debt. After accepting the debt, Shenyang Gaokai had partially realized RMB 4,000,000 of the debt. China Development Bank's claim that the RMB 76,660,000 debt and corresponding interest of Northeast Power Transmission were inferior debts is seriously inconsistent with the objective facts. (b) Regarding the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing: on March 15, 2004, Shenyang Gaokai contributed physical assets appraised at RMB 85,510,600 as capital to jointly establish Cheng Tai Energy with others, thereby holding 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy; on March 24, 2004, Shenyang Gaokai contributed physical assets appraised at RMB 5,747,900 (calculated by subtracting the land use right valued at RMB 155,858,000 from the RMB 161,605,900 alleged by China Development Bank) as capital to jointly establish Xin Tai Warehousing with others, thereby holding 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing. Thus, the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing were together worth approximately RMB 91,258,500. (c) The RMB 76,660,000 debt and interest of Northeast Power Transmission were of comparable value to the 95% equity in Cheng Tai Energy and 95% equity in Xin Tai Warehousing, demonstrating that this equity exchange between Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai was not malicious collusion to harm the interests of third parties. 3. China Development Bank has not provided evidence to prove the existence of malicious collusion between Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai. The transactions between Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai were publicly announced in accordance with the relevant regulations for listed companies and were open market transactions, bearing no relation to malicious collusion as a matter of law. In summary, the appellees request that the court of second instance dismiss China Development Bank's grounds of appeal items 3 and 4.

The defendant at first instance, Shenyang Transformer, agreed with Shenyang Gaokai's response. The defendant at first instance, Northeast Jian'an, did not appear in court.

During the second instance trial, on April 14, 2008, CDB applied to this Court for evidence investigation, requesting that the court of second instance investigate the large-amount inflows and outflows of funds from the Shenyang Dejia account at the Huaxia Bank Jindu Sub-branch during the "equity transaction" period, for the purpose of verifying whether Shenyang Dejia actually paid the 130 million yuan equity transfer price to Shenyang Gaokai. Pursuant to this application, this Court obtained the relevant accounts and found: On November 5, 2006, the book balance of Shenyang Dejia was 499,377.40 yuan; on November 6 of the same year, Liaoning Xintai transferred 130 million yuan to Shenyang Dejia, and Shenyang Dejia paid 130 million yuan to Shenyang Gaokai. On the same day, Shenyang Gaokai endorsed 105,926,302.43 yuan of that amount in two separate amounts to Liaoning Xintai and Liaoning Cheng'an Electric Power Equipment Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cheng'an Electric Power), and Cheng'an Electric Power endorsed it to Liaoning Xintai; on November 7, 2006, Shenyang Gaokai endorsed the remaining 4,761,129.56 yuan to Xintai High Voltage, 9,101,817.50 yuan to Shenyang High Voltage Electrical Product Quality Inspection Co., Ltd., 7,923,341.31 yuan to New Northeast Electric, and 2,287,391.20 yuan to Shenyang Gaodongjia Drying Equipment Co., Ltd. (total 24,073,679.57 yuan). Specifically: 1. Transfer check No. 00304777 from Shenyang Dejia to Shenyang Gaokai, check amount 35,093,768.25 yuan, which Shenyang Gaokai endorsed to Liaoning Xintai; 2. Transfer check No. 00304783 from Shenyang Dejia to Shenyang Gaokai, check amount 70,832,552.18 yuan, which Shenyang Gaokai endorsed to Cheng'an Electric Power, and Cheng'an Electric Power endorsed to Liaoning Xintai; 3. Transfer check No. 00304776 from Shenyang Dejia to Shenyang Gaokai, check amount 4,761,129.56 yuan, which Shenyang Gaokai endorsed to Xintai High Voltage; 4. Transfer check No. 00304778 from Shenyang Dejia to Shenyang Gaokai, check amount 9,101,817.50 yuan, which Shenyang Gaokai endorsed to Shenyang High Voltage Electrical Product Quality Inspection Co., Ltd.; 5. Transfer check No. 00304781 from Shenyang Dejia to Shenyang Gaokai, check amount 7,923,341.31 yuan, which Shenyang Gaokai endorsed to New Northeast Electric; 6. Transfer check No. 00304785 from Shenyang Dejia to Shenyang Gaokai, check amount 2,287,391.20 yuan, which Shenyang Gaokai endorsed to Shenyang Gaodongjia Drying Equipment Co., Ltd. On November 7 of the same year, the book balance of Shenyang Dejia was 49,937.74 yuan, which was the same as the book balance on November 5.

This Court further found that the "Appraisal Report" (Liuhe Zhengxu Appraisal Zi (2002) No. 105) issued by Beijing Liuhe Zhengxu Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. stated that Northeast Electric, in order to verify the asset value of a total of 10 steam turbine generator sets of 120MW and 200MW, commissioned the company to appraise the above assets, and the appraised value was 130.8292 million yuan. Special Notes: 1. For a certain number of equipment, as it was impossible to open and re-inspect each piece, the types and quantities of assets were determined based on the equipment list and packing list provided by the asset possessor. 2. No relevant tests or technical inspections were conducted on the equipment; the appraisers made the appraisal on the assumption that the commissioned equipment could be smoothly installed and used normally. 3. This report shall not be used for any purpose related to movable property, securities, mortgages, investment promotion, or sales. The asset appraisal report (Liao Shenghua Appraisal Zi (2004) No. 017) issued by Liaoning Shenghua Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. had the same commissioning party, appraisal scope, appraisal conclusion, and special notes as the "Appraisal Report" (Liuhe Zhengxu Appraisal Zi (2002) No. 105) issued by Beijing Liuhe Zhengxu Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd.

On December 17, 2002, the Civil (Enforcement) Ruling ([2002] Shen Fa Zhi Zi No. 378) of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province ruled that a third party outside the case would discount the ten steam turbine generator sets at 130 million yuan to offset Northeast Electric's debts. On December 30, 2002, ST Northeast Electric published a major arbitration announcement, the main content of which was the debt situation and debt settlement situation involved in the Civil (Enforcement) Ruling ([2002] Shen Fa Zhi Zi No. 378).

On March 25, 2004, Liaoning Shenghua Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued an asset appraisal report for Northeast Electric with the purpose of verifying asset value. The report stated that the capital verification process did not appraise the value of Northeast Electric's contributed equipment, i.e., the ten steam turbine generator sets, and the equipment valuation was made based on the asset appraisal report Liao Shenghua Appraisal Zi (2004) No. 017 issued by Liaoning Shenghua Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. On March 26, 2004, Northeast Electric invested in Shenyang Tiansheng by discounting the ten steam turbine generator sets at 130 million yuan, holding 98.5% of the equity of Shenyang Tiansheng. On April 8, 2005, Northeast Electric publicly published through the Shenzhen Stock Exchange the "2004 Annual Accounting Statements and Audit Report of Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd." issued by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Certified Public Accountants LLP, which stated that the book value of the ten steam turbine generator sets was 27,878,800 yuan.

On February 17, 2005, the Liaoning Regulatory Bureau of the China Banking Regulatory Commission issued the "Notice on Risk Warning Regarding the Evasion of Bank Debts by Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd." (Liao Yin Jian Fa (2005) No. 42), stating that the bureau had investigated the issue reported by Xinhua News Agency and referred by the CBRC of "Shenyang Gaokai maliciously evading bank debts of hundreds of millions of yuan". After more than two years of careful preparation and thorough implementation, Shenyang Gaokai had emptied the production capacity of a leading enterprise with excellent assets, good performance, normal production and operation, and formed by a large amount of state-owned bank loans, through a series of operations such as investments, transfers, equity changes, and asset swaps, leaving behind huge debts and making it a shell enterprise without debt repayment ability, only possessing a large amount of non-performing assets. Bank loans involving 7 banks and nearly 600 million yuan were stranded, and the methods were egregious and the nature serious.

Opinion of the Court: The focus of the dispute in this case is whether there was a serious value mismatch in Shenyang Gaokai's exchange of its 74.4% equity in Xintai High Voltage for Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng, whether this equity exchange harmed CDB's creditor rights, and whether CDB has the right to exercise the right of revocation against this asset exchange under Article 74 of the Contract Law.

The court of first instance held that Northeast Electric had adduced evidence to prove that on August 13, 2006, Shenyang Gaokai transferred 98.5% of the equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia at a price of 130 million yuan, and therefore there was no issue of serious value mismatch in Shenyang Gaokai's exchange of its 74.4% equity in Xintai High Voltage for Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng. Regarding this determination, the appellant CDB applied to this Court to obtain new evidence. After cross-examination, this Court analyzes and certifies this evidence and other relevant evidence as follows:

1. Regarding the factual finding that Shenyang Gaokai transferred 98.5% of the equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia at a price of 130 million yuan. According to the account records of Shenyang Dejia obtained by this Court, during the "equity transaction" period, the 130 million yuan funds used by Shenyang Dejia to acquire the equity in Shenyang Tiansheng came from Liaoning Xintai. After receiving the 130 million yuan paid by Shenyang Dejia, Shenyang Gaokai on the same day endorsed 105,926,302.43 yuan of it in two separate amounts to Liaoning Xintai and Cheng'an Electric Power, and Cheng'an Electric Power endorsed it to Liaoning Xintai. In this regard, because the 130 million yuan came from Liaoning Xintai, and 80% of the funds were transferred back to Liaoning Xintai on the same day they were withdrawn, CDB claimed that the value of this equity transaction was seriously mismatched. Both Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai argued that Shenyang Gaokai's transfer of 105,926,302.43 yuan was a normal economic exchange between enterprises and could not prove that Shenyang Dejia did not pay the 130 million yuan to Shenyang Gaokai. Given that the reasons of Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric were insufficient to negate the facts found by this Court in the second instance and CDB's appellate ground, in accordance with Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings", this Court required Shenyang Gaokai to adduce evidence to prove the evidentiary materials supporting its rebuttal of CDB's claims. However, within the period for adducing evidence prescribed by this Court, Shenyang Gaokai failed to submit evidence of relevant transaction conduct between the two parties on the grounds that it was unrelated to this case. Therefore, based on the flow of funds in this equity transaction, because 80% of the 130 million yuan equity transaction price was transferred back to the fund issuer Liaoning Xintai on the day of the transaction, CDB's appellate ground that there was a serious value mismatch in the 130 million yuan equity transfer between Shenyang Dejia and Shenyang Gaokai is established. The defenses of Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai that Shenyang Gaokai had received the 130 million yuan equity transaction price paid by Shenyang Dejia are not established due to insufficient evidence.

2. Regarding whether there was a value mismatch in Shenyang Gaokai's exchange of its 74.4% equity in Xintai High Voltage for Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng. According to the facts found in the first and second instances, all parties had no objection that the value of the 74.4% equity in Xintai High Voltage was 130 million yuan, but there was significant dispute over the value of the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng. One piece of evidence submitted by Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric to support that the equity exchange value was equivalent was the capital verification report dated March 25, 2004, issued by Shenyang Liaocheng Accounting Firm regarding Northeast Electric's capital contribution. The report stated that the capital verification process did not appraise the value of the contributed equipment of Northeast Electric to Shenyang Tiansheng, i.e., the ten steam turbine generator sets, and the equipment valuation was made based on the asset appraisal report Liao Shenghua Appraisal Zi (2004) No. 017 issued by Liaoning Shenghua Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. The asset appraisal report Liao Shenghua Appraisal Zi (2004) No. 017 stated: 1. For a certain number of equipment, as it was impossible to open and re-inspect each piece, the types and quantities of assets were determined based on the equipment list and packing list provided by the asset possessor. 2. No relevant tests or technical inspections were conducted on the equipment; the appraisers made the appraisal on the assumption that the commissioned equipment could be smoothly installed and used normally. 3. This report shall not be used for any purpose related to movable property, securities, mortgages, investment promotion, or sales. Regarding the probative force of this appraisal report, this Court holds that the appraisal was commissioned unilaterally by Northeast Electric, not a statutory appraisal issued by a judicial authority commissioning an appraisal institution. The special notes of the appraisal report indicate that the appraisal process did not actually verify the equipment list, nor did it test whether the equipment could be installed and used normally; that is, the appraisal was made without knowing how much equipment actually existed and whether the existing equipment could be used. These practices violated the provisions of the State Administration of State-owned Assets' "Operational Normative Opinions on Asset Appraisal" regarding technical testing and the calculation method of depreciation ratio, and the appraisal conclusion thus derived could not directly and adequately prove the true value of the ten steam turbine generator sets and could not serve as the pricing basis for the transaction of the ten generator sets. Similarly, the "Appraisal Report" (Liuhe Zhengxu Appraisal Zi (2002) No. 105) issued by Beijing Liuhe Zhengxu Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd., submitted by Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric, is also unable to serve as a pricing basis because it is essentially consistent with the asset appraisal report Liao Shenghua Appraisal Zi (2004) No. 017 in terms of formation process and main content.

During the second instance proceedings of this Court, Northeast Electric and Shenyang Gaokai also submitted the Civil (Enforcement) Ruling ([2002] Shen Fa Zhi Zi No. 378) of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province, the "Major Arbitration Announcement of ST Northeast Electric (000585)", and the "Resolution of the 17th Meeting of the Third Board of Directors of Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd." to prove the actual value of the ten steam turbine generator sets. In this regard, this Court holds that the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court, with reference to the "Appraisal Report" (Liuhe Zhengxu Appraisal Zi (2002) No. 105) issued by Beijing Liuhe Zhengxu Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd., ruled that a third party outside the case would discount the ten steam turbine generator sets at 130 million yuan to offset Northeast Electric's debts. Because that Appraisal Report cannot serve as a basis for determining the true value of the ten steam turbine generator sets, this civil ruling can only prove the fact that Northeast Electric lawfully obtained the generator sets, but cannot serve as a basis for determining the true value of the asset, nor can it enhance the probative force of the two appraisal reports. The "Major Arbitration Announcement of ST Northeast Electric (000585)" and the "Resolution of the 17th Meeting of the Third Board of Directors of Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd.", whose main content is to accept this civil ruling, likewise cannot serve as a basis for determining the true value of the ten steam turbine generator sets. According to the "2004 Annual Accounting Statements and Audit Report of Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd." issued by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Certified Public Accountants LLP on April 8, 2005, publicly published by Northeast Electric on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, the book value of the ten generator sets was only 27,878,800 yuan. After a comprehensive analysis and judgment of the above evidence, this Court holds that, given that Northeast Electric's recognized book value for the ten generator sets was 27,878,800 yuan, this value is closer to the cost of Northeast Electric's acquisition of the asset.

In summary, Shenyang Gaokai exchanged its asset worth 130 million yuan for Northeast Electric's asset worth approximately 27,878,800 yuan. Moreover, according to Northeast Electric's publicly published "2004 Annual Accounting Statements and Audit Report of Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd.", Northeast Electric clearly knew that the value of the ten steam turbine generator sets it paid in the transaction with Shenyang Gaokai was only 27,878,800 yuan, yet it still proceeded with the equity exchange with Shenyang Gaokai. This transaction conduct seriously harmed the interests of CDB, a creditor of Shenyang Gaokai. Pursuant to Article 74 of the Contract Law, which provides that "if the debtor transfers property at an obviously unreasonably low price, thereby harming the creditor's interests, and the transferee is aware of the circumstances, the creditor may also request the people's court to revoke the debtor's act", CDB's appellate request to revoke the equity transaction contract between Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric concerning Xintai High Voltage should be supported by this Court. The finding of the first instance judgment that Northeast Electric had paid consideration to Shenyang Gaokai in the equity exchange because Shenyang Gaokai transferred the acquired 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia at a price of 130 million yuan was improper, and this Court hereby corrects it. Given that CDB requests the return of the equity in Shenyang Gaokai obtained by Northeast Electric and, for the part that cannot be returned, compensation for damages, under the principle of mutual restitution, Northeast Electric shall return the 74.4% equity in Xintai High Voltage it obtained to Shenyang Gaokai, and Shenyang Gaokai shall return the 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng it obtained to Northeast Electric. If the two parties cannot mutually return, Northeast Electric shall compensate Shenyang Gaokai for its loss within the range of 130 million yuan minus 27,878,800 yuan.

3. After the court of first instance consolidated the loan dispute it accepted with the revocation dispute transferred by the Liaoning High People's Court for joint trial, CDB did not clearly withdraw the revocation claim. Therefore, based on the facts of the case found, the court of first instance's judgment to revoke the contract for Northeast Electric's exchange of its creditor's rights and interest of RMB 76.66 million against Northeast Transformer with Shenyang Gaokai's 95% equity in Chengtai Energy and 95% equity in Xintai Warehouse was not improper and should be affirmed.

4. Regarding CDB's appellate request that New Northeast Electric, Xintai High Voltage, Chengtai Energy, Xintai Warehouse, and Northeast Electric should bear joint and several liability for Shenyang Gaokai's debts, because New Northeast Electric, Xintai High Voltage, Chengtai Energy, Xintai Warehouse, and Northeast Electric are all independent legal entities and have no connection to the loan relationship between CDB and Shenyang Gaokai. Moreover, the equity exchange transactions between Shenyang Gaokai and Northeast Electric involved in this case have all been revoked, and Shenyang Gaokai's investment rights and interests in Xintai High Voltage, Chengtai Energy, and Xintai Warehouse were not harmed. At the same time, there is no evidence that Shenyang Gaokai's capital contribution to New Northeast Electric affected its liability capacity. Therefore, CDB's appellate request that these four companies should bear joint and several liability within the scope of the property each received lacks factual and legal basis and is not established. As for CDB's appellate request that Northeast Electric should bear joint and several liability for Shenyang Gaokai's debts within the scope of its insufficient registered capital, because CDB failed to provide corresponding evidence, this Court also does not support it.

In summary, except for the incorrect factual finding regarding Shenyang Gaokai's transfer of 98.5% of the equity in Shenyang Tiansheng to Shenyang Dejia at a price of 130 million yuan, the other factual findings of the first instance judgment are clear and the application of law is correct. The appellant CDB's appellate ground regarding the revocation of the contract for Shenyang Gaokai's exchange of its 74.4% equity in Xintai High Voltage for Northeast Electric's 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng is established, and this Court supports it. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. Affirm items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the principal text of the Civil Judgment (2004) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 802 of the Beijing High People's Court.

2. Reverse item 6 of the principal text of said civil judgment.

3. Revoke the contract for Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd.'s exchange of its 74.4% equity in New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High Voltage Disconnector Co., Ltd. (formerly Shenyang Xintai High Voltage Electric Co., Ltd.) for Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd.'s 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng Communication Equipment Co., Ltd.

4. Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, return its 98.5% equity in Shenyang Tiansheng Communication Equipment Co., Ltd. to Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd., and Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, return its 74.4% equity in New Northeast Electric (Shenyang) High Voltage Disconnector Co., Ltd. (formerly Shenyang Xintai High Voltage Electric Co., Ltd.) to Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd. If Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd. and Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd. cannot mutually return, Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd. shall compensate Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd. for its loss within the range of 130 million yuan minus 27,878,800 yuan.

5. Dismiss the other claims of China Development Bank.

The court acceptance fee of RMB 768,729.62 for the first instance and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 759,239.62 shall be borne as per the first instance judgment. The court acceptance fee of RMB 768,729.62 for the second instance shall be borne by Shenyang High Voltage Switch Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 307,491.85, by Northeast Electric Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 307,491.85, and by China Development Bank in the amount of RMB 153,745.92.

The above payments shall be made within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect. If the payment obligation is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

This judgment is final.
